name: Phantasm-VM
target_user: Systems software engineers and compiler developers debugging deterministic execution and reverse step operations.
problem: Debugging low-level assembly or custom bytecode routines is difficult when unexpected state corruption occurs deep in execution loops without time-travel step-back capabilities.
pain: Standard debuggers only step forward, forcing developers to restart execution and reproduce fragile state transitions when chasing obscure memory corruption or stack drift.
solution: A zero-dependency time-travel execution engine and debugger in C11 for a custom 32-bit register-based virtual instruction set, featuring differential state snapshotting, deterministic reverse execution, and page-level memory protection.
verification: Automated test suite asserting opcode decoding accuracy, bit-exact snapshot restoration across 100,000 instruction steps, deterministic step-back verification, and error handling for malformed bytecode frames, unaligned memory access, and stack boundary overflows.
major_features: Custom 32-bit register-based virtual instruction set architecture (ISA) with explicit opcode encoding
Bi-directional execution pipeline supporting step-forward and bit-exact deterministic step-back operations
Page-level copy-on-write memory diffing engine for efficient snapshot state compression
Register-file state checkpoint manager storing execution frames and flags delta histories
Interactive disassembler subsystem converting compiled binary opcode buffers into mnemonic instructions
Breakpoint predicate solver evaluating register and memory expressions before opcode execution
Memory access violation monitor trapping unaligned reads, out-of-bounds writes, and stack overflows
Deterministic instruction replay engine verifying state alignment against logged execution traces
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
